title: Phylogenomics and revision of Proctacanthus (Diptera: Asilidae) north of Mexico
content:
Abstract
The Asilidae are a diverse, monophyletic family of flies. In this study, we analyze the genus Proctacanthus Macquart, by examining over 10,000 specimens from 78 public and private collections and sequencing all but one Proctacanthus species north of Mexico. We recognize 21 species, including 4 new species described herein. We define 2 species groups based on proboscis morphology, which are supported by molecular data: the P. rufiventris species group and the P. philadelphicus species group. Four new species of Proctacanthus are named and described herein: P. arenophilus Mulford & Nelson 2025, sp. nov., P. lyratus Mulford & Nelson 2025, sp. nov., P. hooki Mulford & Nelson 2025, sp. nov., and P. yuma Mulford & Nelson 2025, sp. nov. The entire P. philadelphicus group of 18 species is revised, including P. arenophilus, P. brevipennis, P. coquillettii, P. duryi, P. fulviventris, P. gracilis, P. heros, P. hooki, P. longus, P. lyratus, P. micans, P. milbertii, P. nearno, P. nigriventris, P. nigrofemoratus, P. occidentalis, P. philadelphicus, P. rodecki, and P. yuma. We present a phylogenetic tree generated from whole-genome sequencing data and recover a monophyletic P. rufiventris species group and P. philadelphicus species group. All but one analysis recovered the P. rufiventris group as sister to the rest of Proctacanthus, and P. coquillettii and P. occidentalis as sisters to the rest of the P. philadelphicus group. An analysis of the consensus between morphological characters and molecular data is discussed, and a key to the genus is provided.
